cards.text: Saul, king of Israel, is dead, and David has been anointed king over Judah at Hebron (1 Samuel 31:6; 2 Samuel 2:4). Now ALL the tribes of Israel come to David there. That's a CROWD, friend, and the biggest one I ever got in that junk drawer was one scared can opener sliding in.

cards.question: The tribes of Israel have come to David at Hebron. How do they describe themselves to him?

answers.text: Friends of the house of Jesse

cards.text: Then they bring up the old days, back while Saul was still king over them.

cards.question: Even while Saul was king over them, the tribes say it was ___ who led Israel out and brought them back.

cards.text: And they remind David what the LORD said to him: "You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over them." Friend, you don't forget a word like that.
So the elders of Israel come to King David at Hebron, and he makes a covenant with them before the LORD. Not a handshake, not a thumbs-up in the group chat, a COVENANT!

cards.question: After King David makes a covenant with the elders of Israel at Hebron, what do the elders do?

answers.text: Make him commander of the army
Bring him the crown of Saul

cards.question: David is thirty years old when he becomes king.

cards.text: And David reigns FORTY years, starting with seven years and six months over Judah in Hebron. Friend, I couldn't keep one stamp sharp for forty years!

cards.question: After Hebron, David reigns thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah. From which city?

cards.text: One little problem: Jerusalem isn't David's yet. When David and his men march against the Jebusites who live there, the Jebusites have something to say.

cards.question: As David and his men march on Jerusalem, the Jebusites tell David that even the blind and lame can repel him.

cards.text: They're SO sure, they even think it to themselves: "David cannot get in here." Friend, I said that about my chocolate chip bin once. Famous last words.

cards.question: Nevertheless, David captures the fortress of ___, also known as the City of ___.

cards.text: On that day, David gives the plan for reaching the lame and blind who are despised by David.

cards.question: What does David say whoever attacks the Jebusites must use?

cards.text: That's why people say, "The blind and the lame will never enter the palace." Then David moves into the fortress and calls it the City of David.

cards.question: Once David moves into the fortress, what does he do with the City of David?

answers.text: Builds it up all the way around
Hands it over to the elders

cards.question: From there, David becomes greater and greater, for the LORD God of Hosts was with him.

cards.text: Hiram, king of Tyre, sends envoys to David with cedar logs, carpenters and stonemasons. That's not a little gift, friend, that's a WHOLE construction crew!

cards.question: Hiram's carpenters and stonemasons build a ___ for David.
David realizes the LORD has established him as king and exalted his kingdom for David's own sake.

cards.text: After arriving from Hebron, David takes more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters are born to him. Eleven children born in Jerusalem get named, Nathan and Solomon among them. ELEVEN! I named six stations after my six kids, and David would need a bakery twice the size!
